f1.quote: The WTaVTi precursor was subjected to liquid-metal dealloying by immersion in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h. Ti-rich interdendritic regions were used as preferential sacrificial regions to create a directionally aligned RHEA–Cu composite.

f2.quote: The precursor and Cu were vacuum-sealed in silica and reacted at 1200 °C for 96 h

f3.quote: Irradiation screening used 25 keV He+ implantation up to blistering fluences near 8–8.5 × 10^17 atoms cm−2, with swelling measured by AFM; irradiation behavior was measured on precursor dendrites as a proxy for the eventual RHEA ligaments, not directly on the full composite.

f4.quote: A bicontinuous, directionally aligned structure containing ≈63.6 vol.% BCC RHEA ligaments (W31.5Ta30.9V21.4Ti14.3) and ≈36.4 vol.% nearly pure FCC Cu channels

f5.quote: an approximately 300 nm spontaneously formed W-rich interlayer at every RHEA/Cu interface

f6.quote: Ti has a negative heat of mixing with Cu and preferentially exchanges with Cu and dissolves from the Ti-rich interdendritic channels, whereas W, Ta, and V are comparatively immiscible with Cu and remain as RHEA ligaments.

f7.quote: Continued interfacial Ti extraction leaves W, which has the strongest positive heat of mixing with Cu, trapped as a W-rich passivating interlayer that arrests further exchange and supports stable bonding.

f8.quote: Aligned Cu channels provide conductive pathways; the increase in thermal conductivity with temperature is attributed to reduced diffuse interfacial mismatch and increasing lattice-mediated transport overcoming declining electronic transport.

f9.quote: Relative to the low-conductivity WTaVTi precursor, Cu-channel formation was expected to raise thermal conductivity substantially, particularly at high temperature, ultimately allowing the composite to surpass pure W

f11.quote: relative to pure W, the WTaVTi RHEA ligaments were expected to show lower He-induced swelling and delayed blistering.
